title: Noisy online opposition to AUKUS doesn’t equal real-world opposition | The Strategist
paragraphs: The report of the so-called independent public inquiry into AUKUS, and the subsequent reaction to it on social media, offer a troubling insight into the state of Australian public debate.

The ‘inquiry’ received more than 1,000 submissions and recommended abandoning Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine program. Its organisers reported 83,000 downloads of the final report within 24 hours. Online, the intensity of opposition to AUKUS and the certainty of many commentators could leave readers believing that Australians had overwhelmingly rejected AUKUS. Yet the Lowy Institute’s 2026 polling found that 68 percent of Australians supported acquiring nuclear-powered submarines, while only 29 percent opposed them.

The contrast exposes a growing weakness in Australian public debate. We’re confusing the intensity of participation with the breadth of public support, and personal conviction with established fact. More concerning is how these misunderstandings can influence what political leaders believe Australians want.
